top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a genuine discovery about how interacting quantum systems organise themselves: the Bose-Hubbard model realised in optical lattices, the superfluid-to-Mott transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site imaging, with quantitative agreement with many-body theory and two decades of reproduction in many laboratories. The experimental trio of Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger matches the observations the citation names, avoiding singling out one author of the joint 1998 proposal; the unreached doped Hubbard regime is a caveat but does not undo the Mott and microscopy results. P003 follows as the cleaner, bounded and thoroughly reproduced result, though it delivers a capability and tighter limits more than a new fact about nature.
recusal_note: Long-time collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, plus Schuch and Indelicato; none is credited in any proposal, and no direct tie to Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Katori, Ye or the other laureates is apparent from the profile. Atomic physics proximity to P001 and P003 is not a formal conflict.
